source_metadata.title: A three-metabolite microbiota-associated signature for early risk stratification of gestational diabetes mellitus

atoms.canonical_statement: The study aimed to identify first-trimester serum metabolite biomarkers associated with subsequent GDM risk, integrate supportive gut metagenomic findings, and develop and validate an early-pregnancy prediction model.

The study used a multistage, multicenter design with retrospective nested case-control phases for biomarker discovery, replication, and model development, followed by independent external and prospective validation phases.
From January through December 2024, 2,693 pregnant women were enrolled across three hospitals in China.

population.label: Pregnant women enrolled across three hospitals in China

atoms.canonical_statement: Eligible participants were 18-45 years old, had singleton pregnancies, completed prenatal registration in early pregnancy, and had complete clinical information and qualified biospecimens.

Women with pregestational diabetes, prior GDM, multiple pregnancy, major pregnancy complications, recent medications affecting metabolism or gut microbiota, severe systemic disorders, malignancy, or incomplete data were excluded.

population.label: Excluded pregnant participants
exclusion_criteria: Recent medication affecting metabolism or gut microbiota

atoms.canonical_statement: GDM was diagnosed at 24-28 gestational weeks by a 75-g OGTT using 2020 ADA thresholds: fasting glucose >=5.1 mmol/L, 1-hour glucose >=10.0 mmol/L, or 2-hour glucose >=8.5 mmol/L.

outcome.definition: Any of fasting >=5.1 mmol/L, 1-h >=10.0 mmol/L, or 2-h >=8.5 mmol/L after 75-g OGTT at 24-28 weeks

atoms.canonical_statement: 92 GDM cases and 88 healthy controls at Nanjing Maternity and Child Health Care Hospital; first- and second-trimester serum, with second-trimester fecal samples in a subset.
50 GDM cases and 70 healthy controls at Zhongda Hospital, Southeast University; first-trimester serum; replication/model development.
48 GDM cases and 49 healthy controls at Changzhou Maternity and Child Health Care Hospital; first-trimester serum; replication/model development.
96 GDM cases and 81 healthy controls at Nanjing Maternity and Child Health Care Hospital; first-trimester serum; independent validation only.
76 GDM cases and 76 healthy controls at Changzhou Maternity and Child Health Care Hospital; first-trimester serum; independent validation only.

335 consecutively recruited pregnant women at Zhongda Hospital, Southeast University; 55 subsequently developed GDM and 280 remained normoglycemic; first-trimester serum was collected before diagnosis.

Biomarker discovery and candidate-metabolite selection were restricted to the discovery and independent replication cohorts; the external and prospective cohorts were reserved exclusively for validation to limit information leakage.

Untargeted serum metabolomics used UHPLC-high-resolution mass spectrometry in positive- and negative-ion modes, followed by feature processing, missing-value imputation, normalization, and metabolite annotation; the three selected metabolites were then quantified by targeted LC-MS/MS with internal-standard correction and calibration.

Second-trimester fecal samples from 32 women with GDM and 32 healthy controls in the discovery cohort underwent metagenomic sequencing; downstream analyses included taxonomic abundance, diversity, co-occurrence networks, and multi-omics Spearman correlations.

The targeted development dataset pooled 190 GDM cases and 207 healthy controls from the discovery and two independent cohorts, then used stratified random sampling to create 70% training and 30% internal-validation subsets.

Within the training cohort, GLM, random forest, and support vector machine models were compared using repeated 10-fold cross-validation with three repeats and AUC as the primary performance metric; formal comparison used a Friedman test followed by Holm-corrected pairwise Wilcoxon signed-rank tests.

atoms.canonical_statement: The final GLM was fit in the training cohort, the Youden index selected a probability cutoff of 0.368, and the locked model plus the fixed cutoff and training-derived scaling parameters were applied unchanged to internal, external, and prospective validation cohorts.

atoms.canonical_statement: Clinical benchmarking compared a clinical-only model using maternal age, first-trimester BMI, and gestational week at sampling; the three-metabolite model; and a combined clinical-plus-metabolite model across all cohorts.
In the first trimester, mean BMI was 23.64 in women who later developed GDM versus 21.16 in healthy controls (P=0.050).

atoms.canonical_statement: In the first trimester, mean triglycerides were 1.77 mmol/L in women who later developed GDM versus 1.47 mmol/L in healthy controls (P=0.008).

atoms.canonical_statement: In the first trimester, mean platelet count was 236.98 x10^9/L in women who later developed GDM versus 229.33 x10^9/L in healthy controls (P=0.023).

population.label: Discovery cohort, first trimester: 92 future GDM cases and 88 healthy controls

atoms.canonical_statement: OPLS-DA showed separation of serum metabolic profiles between GDM and healthy-control groups in both the first and second trimesters.
First-trimester untargeted metabolomics detected 2,751 features and identified 131 differential metabolites (76 upregulated and 55 downregulated) using adjusted P<0.05 and VIP>1.

concept.text: Differential serum metabolites in first trimester

atoms.canonical_statement: Second-trimester untargeted metabolomics detected 2,686 features and identified 118 differential metabolites (79 upregulated and 39 downregulated) using the study screening criteria.

concept.text: Differential serum metabolites in second trimester

atoms.canonical_statement: Intersection of first- and second-trimester differential metabolites identified 14 metabolites with persistent directional changes across gestation: 10 upregulated and 4 downregulated.

population.label: Discovery cohort across first and second trimesters

concept.text: Persistently differential serum metabolites across gestation

atoms.canonical_statement: The 14 persistent metabolites had individual AUCs ranging from 0.700 to 0.973 for GDM discrimination in the first trimester.
The 14 persistent metabolites had individual AUCs ranging from 0.665 to 0.957 for GDM discrimination in the second trimester.
In the second-trimester metagenomic subset, alpha diversity and beta diversity did not differ significantly between GDM and healthy-control groups at genus or species level.
Odoribacter splanchnicus was less abundant in the GDM group, with log2 fold change -1.63 (P=4.8e-05).
Paraprevotella clara was less abundant in the GDM group, with log2 fold change -1.36 (P=0.0011).
Bacteroides eggerthii was less abundant in the GDM group, with log2 fold change -1.2 (P=0.0022).

Five species with degree >=15 in both GDM and healthy-control co-occurrence networks—Bacteroides eggerthii, Odoribacter splanchnicus, Bacteroides thetaiotaomicron, Paraprevotella clara, and Bacteroides clarus—were retained as shared high-connectivity taxa, and all five had lower abundance in GDM.
Representative genera and species generally showed inverse correlations with fasting blood glucose and triglycerides, with some also inversely associated with BMI.

The five representative species showed broadly concordant metabolite associations: generally positive associations with propionic acid and formylkynurenine and negative associations with gamma-Glu-Leu, 3-hydroxydecanoic acid, and several other persistent metabolites.

Across the discovery and two independent first-trimester cohorts, 3-hydroxydecanoic acid and gamma-Glu-Leu were consistently elevated and propionic acid was consistently reduced; the three were retained for targeted model construction because of cross-cohort consistency and temporal stability.

Repeated cross-validation produced mean AUCs of 0.854+/-0.044 for random forest, 0.837+/-0.061 for GLM, and 0.845+/-0.067 for SVM; the overall Friedman test found no significant algorithm difference (P=0.216).

population.label: Training cohort from pooled targeted development dataset

atoms.canonical_statement: The locked three-metabolite GLM achieved an AUC of 0.838 (95% CI 0.791-0.885) in the Training cohort; accuracy 0.758, sensitivity 0.854, specificity 0.673, balanced accuracy 0.764.

atoms.canonical_statement: Compared with random forest, the final GLM did not differ significantly in internal validation (P=0.712) but significantly outperformed random forest in both external validation cohorts and the prospective cohort after Holm correction.

atoms.canonical_statement: In the Training cohort, the clinical-only model AUC was 0.671, the three-metabolite model AUC was 0.838, and the combined model AUC was 0.853; the combined model did not significantly improve AUC over the metabolite-only model (DeLong P=0.137).

In the Internal validation cohort, the clinical-only model AUC was 0.649, the three-metabolite model AUC was 0.840, and the combined model AUC was 0.849; the combined model did not significantly improve AUC over the metabolite-only model (DeLong P=0.228).

In the External validation cohort 1, the clinical-only model AUC was 0.695, the three-metabolite model AUC was 0.955, and the combined model AUC was 0.962; the combined model did not significantly improve AUC over the metabolite-only model (DeLong P=0.316).

In the External validation cohort 2, the clinical-only model AUC was 0.667, the three-metabolite model AUC was 0.917, and the combined model AUC was 0.926; the combined model did not significantly improve AUC over the metabolite-only model (DeLong P=0.284).

In the Prospective cohort, the clinical-only model AUC was 0.683, the three-metabolite model AUC was 0.969, and the combined model AUC was 0.975; the combined model did not significantly improve AUC over the metabolite-only model (DeLong P=0.341).
BMI remained associated with GDM in the multivariable logistic regression (OR 1.202; 95% CI 1.091-1.325; P<0.001).

atoms.canonical_statement: The authors concluded that early and persistent metabolic perturbation and coordinated microbiota-associated metabolite changes can support early-pregnancy GDM risk stratification using a compact three-metabolite panel.

The authors stated that the panel should currently be viewed as an early risk-stratification tool rather than a standalone diagnostic test, because the prospective cohort had high AUC and NPV but only moderate PPV.
Gut microbiome data were available only in the second trimester, limiting assessment of early-pregnancy microbial dynamics and temporal alignment with first-trimester metabolomics.
Pregnancy-related physiological metabolic adaptation may contribute to observed metabolite shifts, in addition to GDM-related changes.
The clinical benchmark did not fully incorporate dietary patterns, lifestyle factors, family history of diabetes, genetic background, or detailed obstetric history.
The study population was drawn predominantly from coastal Eastern China, limiting geographic and ethnic generalizability.
Postpartum metabolic and cardiovascular outcomes were not available, so the study cannot determine whether the panel predicts long-term cardiometabolic outcomes after pregnancy.
The observational microbiome-metabolite analyses cannot establish causality between microbial taxa, circulating metabolites, and GDM development.
AUC assesses discrimination rather than absolute calibration; higher AUCs in external cohorts do not necessarily imply superior clinical transportability.
